mentions.note: ten years ago (1927-28): first Belgrave man home, 63rd, in the "National" at Leamington
1928: won the Two Miles (North) in North v. South match
helped flag the course on winter Saturdays
ran the final stage into Brighton in the 1932 London to Brighton Relay (3rd); captain; Life Membership at the 1936 A.G.M.
Captain; held third place to the end 1932
printed "Bill and Frank Webb" and "Frank and Bill Webb"; 1930s member at the funeral
member who used the old Battersea Park track (three laps to the mile); address given as Teddington

mentions.h: Pleased there was no change of name

photos.c: Our picture shows four of the club's elder statesmen in a relaxed mood during this year's Centenary Club '20' road race. ... They are (left to right) :- Ken O'Kell (86) - 64 years a member, Bill Webb (93) - 60 years a member, Frank Webb (84) - 59 years a member, Norman Dewberry (85) - 59 years a member

Bill Webb has got an "ology" - Campanology - as he inaugurates the "Centenary Bell" which bears the inscription: "This bell was unveiled by the most Senior past President - W.G.Webb - on the 100th Birthday of the Club 7 October 1987". The Bell was donated by Chas.Manning Past President.
